finding.shortLabel: Two Gurney lot-holders at post-1667 Mendon: the son and the widow
finding.statement: The post-1667 Mendon proprietors' records preserve two separate Gurney lot-holders of the same generation: John Gurny, matching the resident son John Jr., whose twenty-acre lot passed out of the family by sale in 1692; and Grisel Gurny, John Sr.'s widow, holding her own twenty-acre lot in her own right and willing it to her son by an earlier marriage, Joseph Juell. The two records track the family's already-established son-who-settled-there and widow-who-remarried-elsewhere lines, not a single household.

finding.statement: The Mendon proprietors' records list "Grisel Gurney, a twenty acre lot" as a separate purchaser from John Gurny, and carry a copy of her will, returned to the town through guardians in Chelmsford, in which "the Widdow Gurny that Was And Last of all Wife to the Abouesd John Burge" left her Mendon accommodation to her son Joseph Juell, with payments due Nathanil Juell, Mercy Juell, and Sherabiah Keby.
